affordance_in_statement: You must establish a single dispatch sequence (a permutation of the j trains). Both security teams will process the trains in this exact same chosen order. ... Formally, if we let s_k and c_k be the Structural and Cargo duration times of the k-th train in your chosen sequence, ... A_k = A_{k-1} + s_k ... B_k = max(A_k, B_{k-1}) + c_k
secondary_shortcut_name: Direct exposure of the two-machine recurrence
removal_suggestion: Preserve the same semantics, but replace the explicit A_k/B_k recurrence and the terminology of two sequential teams with an indirect event-timeline description: each train's second inspection starts when both that train is released and the second team's previous inspection has finished. Avoid presenting the problem in the canonical two-machine flow-shop form.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the standard Johnson partition and sorting rule.

common_affordance: The statement explicitly defines a two-machine permutation flow shop through a common job order and the standard machine-completion recurrence, making Johnson's rule immediately recognizable.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It sorts by (s - c) descending, which is not Johnson's partition-and-sort rule and is not generally optimal.

recommended_edit: Re-present the scheduling semantics as an indirect freight-depot event timeline, removing the explicit machine labels, permutation-flow-shop terminology, and A_k/B_k recurrence while retaining exactly the same constraints and objective.
